newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Hot junk market rises broadly.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Hot junk market rises broadly.

text.p: Prices in the high-yield market rose broadly on Thursday, charged by euphoria over new issues and a rally in the Treasury market, traders said.
Wall Street firms sold over $1.5 billion in new junk bond issues on Thursday. Many issues were increased in size as dealers scrambled to fill orders from customers.
Such strength in new issues helped generate healthy buying activity, pushing prices in the secondary market up 3/8 to 5/8 of a point, traders said.
Meanwhile, the high-grade market was calmer, with prices remaining largely unchanged on modest volume.
Fox/Liberty Networks priced the largest deal of the day -- a whopping $750 million two-part issue via Merrill Lynch & Co.
The company increased the deal's senior note tranche to $500 million from an original amount of $350 million.

Elsewhere, Central European Media Enterprises upsized a rare offering of mark-denominated junk bonds to 140 million marks from 100 million marks. Morgan Stanley priced the securities to yield 8.125 percent or 312.5 basis points over the seven-year bund.
Market players said the deal highlights the growing demand for high-yield securities from European investors.
The company also sold $100 million of dollar-denominated junk bonds to yield 9.375 percent or 312.5 basis points over the seven-year Treasury.
IXC Communications Inc increased an offering of junior exchangeable PIK preferred stock to $300 million from an original size of $200 million.
Credit Suisse First Boston priced the deal at par to yield 12.5 percent.
European telecom start-up Hermes Railtel B.V. also found success with its debut offering via DLJ. The issue was increased to $265 million from $175 million.

In secondary market activity, Diamond Cable Communications 10 3/4 percent zero coupon bonds due '07 rose 1 1/4 points to 62-62 1/2 on stronger-than-expected earnings report release yesterday, a trader said.
Also, Iridium LLC bonds 13 percent units rose 2.5 points to 106 1/2, triggered by a rise in the company's stock. Iridium stock rose 2.5 points to 34 3/8.

Brunos Inc bonds continued to come under selling pressure, following a dissappointing earnings release earlier this week. The company's bonds were quoted 95-97 on Thursday, down three points from Tuesday.

Speedy Muffler King 10 7/8 percent notes due '06 closed at 90-94, dropping four points from yesterday's closing level, traders said. They said the weakness was due to follow-through selling after the company released dissappointing earnings earlier this week.
In the high-grade sector, spreads on Columbia/HCA Healthcare bonds continued to widen on Thursday as concerns grew about the federal investigation of the company.
Spreads on Columbia's 30-year bonds closed at 130-120 basis points, which was roughly 20-25 basis points wider than levels from late last week.
"When you get news coming across the tape that (the company) could lose their certification with Medicare, then I don't think anyone wants to be a hero," said one trader.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 13.71 to close at 7942.3
Treasury prices rallied as the Consumer Price Index and industrial production and capacity utilization data confirmed that visible signs of a pickup in inflation were nowhere to be seen.
The price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 31/32 to close at 97-23/32, pushing its yield down to 6.55 percent.
-Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-895-1662
